title: Curved geometry, mesh generation and conservative transfer

items.title: Intersection-volume conservative remapping
items.statement: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable domain of finite positive measure. Let $\mathcal S=(S_i)_{i=1}^m$ and $\mathcal T=(T_j)_{j=1}^n$ be finite measurable partitions of $\Omega$ up to null sets, with disjoint interiors modulo null sets and positive cell volumes. Define exact overlap weights $w_{ji}=|T_j\cap S_i|$. For source constants $v_i$, the intersection-volume remap is the target piecewise-constant field $Rv$ whose value on $T_j$ is $ (Rv)_j=|T_j|^{-1}\sum_i w_{ji}v_i$. All weights are exact measures; an approximate clipping weight is not silently substituted.

items.title: Admissible isoparametric curved cells
items.statement: Fix a reference matching affine simplicial mesh as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. An admissible curved cell is the image of a closed reference simplex $\widehat K$ under a map $F_K\in C^2(\widehat K;\mathbb R^d)$ that extends to a diffeomorphism on a neighborhood, is orientation preserving, and satisfies $0<j_0\le J_K:=\det DF_K\le j_1$ and $\|DF_K\|+\|(DF_K)^{-1}\|+\|D^2F_K\|\le C_F$. The physical cells have disjoint interiors, cover the domain up to their shared facets, and maps agree on each common reference facet under the prescribed affine facet identification. Define the volume metric $G_K=DF_K^TDF_K$, volume factor $J_K=\sqrt{\det G_K}$, and for a reference facet parametrization $\widehat f$ the surface metric $G_{K,\widehat f}=D(F_K\circ\widehat f)^TD(F_K\circ\widehat f)$ and surface factor $\sqrt{\det G_{K,\widehat f}}$. The positive-Jacobian lower bound is the admissibility certificate; it is not inferred from a drawing or from Delaunay quality.

items.title: The nodal P1 interpolant preserves homogeneous boundary values
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ have a finite matching affine triangular mesh, and let $u\in H^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\cap H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. On each triangle take the unique continuous representative of the restriction of $u$. These representatives give one well-defined value at every mesh vertex. The global nodal P1 interpolant $I_hu$, affine on each triangle and equal to these values at its vertices, is continuous, has zero trace on every boundary edge, and belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$.

items.title: Curved-domain geometry approximation errors
items.statement: Let $\widehat\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded reference domain and let $\Phi,\Phi_h:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\mathbb R^d$ be cellwise $C^2$ admissible maps with matching traces, positive Jacobians, and common image topology. The exact and approximate domains are $\Omega=\Phi(\widehat\Omega)$ and $\Omega_h=\Phi_h(\widehat\Omega)$. Define $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega)}$ and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega;op)}$. A geometry approximation claim must separately state bounds on $e_0,e_1$, both Jacobian lower bounds, and boundary-trace compatibility; none follows from the word “isoparametric.”

items.title: P1 interpolation scaling on uniformly curved cells
items.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice. In dimension two let $K=\Psi(\widetilde K)$, where $\widetilde K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle of diameter comparable to $h_K$, and $\Psi$ extends to a $C^2$ diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of $\overline{\widetilde K}$. Assume $\|D\Psi\|_\infty+\|D\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty+\|D^2\Psi\|_\infty+\|J_\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty$ are uniformly bounded. Let $v$ denote its continuous representative and set $I_Kv=(I_{\widetilde K}(v\circ\Psi))\circ\Psi^{-1}$, the mapped nodal P1 interpolant. For $v\in H^2(K)$, $\|v-I_Kv\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^2\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$ and $|v-I_Kv|_{H^1(K)}\le C h_K\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$, with $C$ uniform over the family.

items.title: Pullback gradients and induced surface metrics
Overlap remapping is an L2 projection, conservative and positive
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Under the finite partition hypotheses of [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]], let $P_0(\mathcal T)$ be the target cellwise-constant subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. For every source piecewise-constant $v$, $Rv$ is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $v$ onto $P_0(\mathcal T)$, hence $\|Rv\|_2\le\|v\|_2$. It preserves total mass, $\int_\Omega Rv=\int_\Omega v$, and if all $v_i\ge0$ then every target value $(Rv)_j\ge0$.

items.title: Geometry error bounds a pulled-back boundary-lift residual
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ be covered by a finite matching cell mesh, and let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be continuous geometry maps whose cellwise $C^1$ derivatives satisfy $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$, $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_\infty$, and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty;op}$. Let $G$ be a scalar physical boundary lift on an open convex neighborhood containing both images and every segment joining corresponding image points, with $\|DG\|_\infty\le L_1$ and $\|D^2G\|_\infty\le L_2$. Define the piecewise pullback gradients by $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)=D\Phi^T
abla G(\Phi)$ and $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h)=D\Phi_h^T
abla G(\Phi_h)$, and set $$\ell_{\partial,h}(w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega} ig(
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)-
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h) ig)\cdot
abla w,\qquad w\in H^1_0(\widehat\Omega).$$ With the $H^1$ dual norm, $\|\ell_{\partial,h}\|_{(H^1_0)^*}\le 2(L_1e_1+ML_2e_0)$. Thus the geometry-induced boundary-lift contribution to the Strang load defect is $O(e_0+e_1)$.

items.title: Cofactor, surface-Jacobian, and normal perturbation bounds
items.statement: Let $A=D\Phi$ and $A_h=D\Phi_h$ be orientation-preserving cell-map derivatives with $\det A,\det A_h\ge j_*>0$, $\|A\|_{op},\|A_h\|_{op}\le M$, and $\|A-A_h\|_{op}\le e_1$. For every unit reference-facet normal $\widehat n$, define the surface Jacobians $J_\Gamma(A)=\|\operatorname{cof}(A)\widehat n\|$, $J_\Gamma(A_h)=\|\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\widehat n\|$, and mapped unit normals $n_\Gamma(A)=\operatorname{cof}(A)\widehat n/J_\Gamma(A)$ and $n_\Gamma(A_h)=\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\widehat n/J_\Gamma(A_h)$. Then $$\|\operatorname{cof}(A)-\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\|_{op}+|J_\Gamma(A)-J_\Gamma(A_h)|+|n_\Gamma(A)-n_\Gamma(A_h)|\le C(d,M,j_*)e_1.$$ The surface Jacobian agrees with the Gram-metric factor in [[def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map]].

items.title: Derivative geometry error controls the Laplace tensor defect
items.statement:
Let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be the orientation-preserving maps of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], with $J,J_h\ge j_*>0$ and $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$. Set $B=J D\Phi^{-1}D\Phi^{-T}$ and $B_h=J_hD\Phi_h^{-1}D\Phi_h^{-T}$. Then $\|B-B_h\|_\infty\le C e_1$, where $C$ depends only on $d,j_*,M$. Consequently $|\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^T(B-B_h)
abla w|\le C e_1\|
abla v\|_2\|
abla w\|_2$ for $v,w\in H^1(\widehat\Omega)$.

items.title: P1 approximation of a parabolic shear map
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=[-1,1]^2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a matching shape-regular affine triangulation, and put $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. Let $I_h$ be the vertexwise P1 interpolant and $\Phi_h(x,y)=(x,y+I_h(x^2/4))$. In the notation of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], there is a constant $C$ depending only on the shape-regularity bound such that $e_0\le Ch^2$ and $e_1\le Ch$. For sufficiently small $h$, $\det D\Phi_h\ge1/2$, and $\Phi_h$ is globally one-to-one on the square. The exact map has $\det D\Phi=1$ and a global inverse $(X,Y)\mapsto(X,Y-X^2/4)$.

items.title: Remap error separates source, target and geometry approximation
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega$ be bounded, let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be the geometry maps of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]] and assume each is a global orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism from $\widehat\Omega$ onto its image, with $J_h\le J^*$ and $u$ is $L_u$-Lipschitz on the union of their images. On $\Omega_h=\Phi_h(\widehat\Omega)$ let $\mathcal S,\mathcal T$ be finite positive-volume partitions and let $v_S$ be source-piecewise-constant data with finite $L^2$ error. Assume the exact target projection error below is finite. Define $P_Tq$ on each target cell by its exact cell average, $\eta_S=\|u-v_S\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$, and $\eta_T=\|u-P_Tu\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$. If $R$ is the exact overlap remap, then\n$$\|u\circ\Phi-(Rv_S)\circ\Phi_h\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega,J_h)}\le L_u e_0\sqrt{J^*|\widehat\Omega|}+\eta_S+\eta_T,$$\nwhere $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_\infty$ and $\|z\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega,J_h)}^2=\int_{\widehat\Omega}|z|^2J_h$.

items.title: Conforming NVB closure preserves curved shared traces
items.statement: Let a compatible labeled reference triangulation be refined by recursive reference-edge closure as in [[alg-dorfler-marking-and-conforming-nvb-refinement]]. The closure terminates in a matching conforming affine descendant. If every cell is mapped through one common injective geometry map whose traces agree on common reference facets, the resulting curved cells also have matching interfaces.

items.title: Strang error bound for a parabolic isoparametric P1 family
Exact certified clipping of convex rational polygons
items.statement: Input two finite, positive-area convex polygons $P,Q\subset\mathbb Q^2$ with rational vertices listed cyclically; output their exact rational intersection polygon and its exact area, or `unresolved` if a required orientation sign or convexity condition cannot be certified. Normalize each polygon to counterclockwise order by exact signed area. For each directed edge of $Q$, clip the current cyclic vertex list of $P$ to its closed left half-plane. Evaluate each orientation exactly: clear a common positive denominator from the rational coordinates and call [[alg-certified-dyadic-geometric-predicate]] on the resulting integer (hence dyadic) coordinates. For a crossing segment $S E$, insert the exact rational intersection $S+t(E-S)$ with $t=s(S)/(s(S)-s(E))$, where $s(X)$ is the signed edge determinant. Remove consecutive duplicate vertices after each pass. Return zero area for fewer than three noncollinear output vertices; otherwise compute the shoelace area exactly. No floating tolerance is used.

items.title: Certified clipping returns the exact convex polygon overlap
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For rational positive-area convex polygons $P,Q$ whose required orientation signs are certified, [[alg-certified-convex-polygon-overlap]] terminates and returns exactly $P\cap Q$ as a cyclic rational polygon, with its exact Lebesgue area. Empty intersections and intersections consisting only of a point or segment return area zero. The result can be used as the exact weight $|P\cap Q|$ in [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]].

items.title: Delaunay-seeded curved uniform NVB refinement
items.statement: Input the exact dyadic square $[-1,1]^2$, a tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, and the exact shear $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. The boundary features are the four closed edges and four vertices; features are incident when their sets intersect, and separation is the minimum Euclidean distance between nonincident feature sets. Record the interior boundary-angle certificate $\alpha=\pi/2$ and the nonincident-feature separation certificate $\sigma=1$. Run exact planar Delaunay insertion on the four square corners. Verify its output consists of two triangles sharing a diagonal; label that diagonal reference on both triangles and label the boundary edges nonreference. Set $k=0$. While $(3/2)2^{-k}(2\sqrt2)>\tau$, set $\eta_K^2=1$, $o_K^2=0$ on every current cell and call [[alg-dorfler-marking-and-conforming-nvb-refinement]] with $\theta_E=1$, $\theta_O=1$. Start the cycle budget at $B=1$; if the call returns `budget-exhausted`, retry from the unchanged mesh with $B$ doubled until it returns `complete`. A complete call requests three generations on every cell and uses recursive conformity closure; then set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and test the diameter bound again. Map every output reference triangle by the common shear $\Phi$ and return the mapped cells, feature certificates, and $k$. If a predicate is unresolved, the Delaunay seed does not have the stated two-triangle form, or closure returns invalid input, return `unresolved`.

items.title: Quality and finite termination for the curved square NVB family
items.statement: For every tolerance $0<\tau\le\sigma/4=1/4$, the algorithm [[alg-delaunay-seeded-curved-uniform-nvb-refinement]] with square boundary angle $\alpha=\pi/2$ and nonincident-feature separation $\sigma=1$ terminates after finitely many three-generation cycles. Its reference triangles remain right isosceles with minimum angle $\pi/4$, all interfaces match, and every curved cell map is orientation preserving with mapped metric condition number at most $9/4$ times the reference-cell condition number. The returned maximum curved-cell diameter is at most $\tau$. This is a guarantee for this square/shear family; it asserts no general Delaunay minimum-angle theorem, adaptive complexity bound, or 3D shape bound.

title: Curved geometry, mesh generation and conservative transfer — Examples

items.title: An orientation-reversing cell fails the Jacobian certificate
items.statement: Take the reference triangle with vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)$ and the affine map $F(x,y)=(y,x)$. Its Jacobian determinant is $-1$, so it cannot satisfy the admissibility condition $J_F\ge j_0>0$.

items.title: Opposite diagonals conserve mass under a curved shear
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Map $[-1,1]^2$ by the area-preserving shear $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. Triangulate the square once along the southwest-to-northeast diagonal and once along the other diagonal; map both meshes by the same $\Phi$. Every source-target overlap has area $1$. If the source cell values are $2$ and $0$, each target average is $1$, source and target total mass are both $4$, and all target values remain nonnegative.

items.title: A ten-cell isoparametric mesh exactly covers the unit disk
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $a=1/2$ and $g(t)=a\tan(\pi t/4)$. Map the reference square $[-1,1]^2$ to the central square $[-a,a]^2$ by $H(t,q)=(g(t),g(q))$ and split it into two triangles. For the top annular sector use $\theta(t)=\pi/2-\pi t/4$, $r(s,t)=(1-s)a/\sin\theta(t)+s$, and $F(t,s)=r(s,t)(\cos\theta(t),\sin\theta(t))$; split this rectangle into two triangles and rotate it for the other three sides. These ten mapped triangles have positive Jacobians, matching traces, and union equal to the closed unit disk.

items.title: An empty-sphere tetrahedron can be arbitrarily flat
items.statement: For $0<\varepsilon<1$, take $p_1=(0,0,0)$, $p_2=(1,0,0)$, $p_3=(0,1,0)$, and $p_4=(1/4,1/4,\varepsilon)$. They span one tetrahedron. Its circumsphere is empty of other sites because there are no other sites, so it is a Delaunay tetrahedron, while its inradius tends to zero and its diameter is at least $1$.

items.title: A parabolic shear has certified linear geometry approximations
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $[-1,1]^2$, the exact shear $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$ maps each straight reference edge to a straight or parabolic arc. Its determinant is $1$. On any shape-regular affine mesh, the nodal P1 geometry map satisfies $e_0\le Ch^2$, $e_1\le Ch$, and $J_h\ge1/2$ for small enough $h$. Consequently its Laplace tensor differs from the exact pulled-back tensor by at most $Ch$ in $L^\infty$.
